functional.text: Viewers post a short comment (≤ 200 characters) on a live video.
Viewers of a live video see other viewers' new comments in real time.
A viewer who joins late sees the most recent ~50 comments at once; comments are kept for replay with the recording.
Moderation: blocked words are filtered when posting; the streamer or a moderator can delete a comment and it disappears from screens.

non_functional.text: A comment appears on other viewers' screens within 2 s at p99.
Hot streams: one video may have 5M concurrent viewers and 10k comments/s, and must not slow down other videos.
Available and durable: a posted comment is never lost from storage, but showing a sample of comments live on a hot stream is acceptable.

assumptions.text: 20M concurrent viewers at peak across ~100k live videos; a viewer comments about once every 10 minutes.
~300 B stored per comment; people read at most ~10 comments/s.

out_of_scope.text: Video ingest and streaming, reactions/likes, threaded replies.

api.notes: Acked once appended to the log; client_comment_id dedups retries.
One long-lived stream per viewer; the client shows its own comment immediately.
Called on join; cached at the CDN for 1 s.
Moderators only; emits a tombstone event through the same log.

data.name: comments
data.fields: video_id + hour bucket (partition key), comment_id (time-ordered, clustering), user_id, text, status (visible|deleted), ts
data.why: Append-only, read by video and time range for replay; ~100 TB/year.

data.name: recent_comments
data.fields: video_id → list of the last 50 comments
data.why: What every joiner reads; tiny and hot.

data.name: subscriptions
data.fields: in each gateway's memory: video_id → local connections; in Redis: channel video:{id} → subscribed gateways
data.why: Routing is per gateway, never per viewer.

parts.title: Comment ingestion and storage
parts.problem: Accept ~33k comments/s at peak (10k/s on one hot video), filter them, and acknowledge only once the comment can't be lost, while both real-time delivery and long-term storage get every comment.

options.name: Write to SQL; readers poll it
options.cons: every viewer's poll hits the database; one table takes 33k writes/s

options.name: Write to the database, then publish to delivery
options.cons: dual write: a crash between the two loses the publish or shows comments that were never stored

options.name: Log first: append to a replicated log keyed by video_id, ack, and let persisters and dispatchers consume independently
options.pros: one durable write on the hot path; delivery and storage can't disagree; each consumer lags or retries alone
options.cons: storage is eventually consistent (seconds); needs a log cluster

parts.choice: Log first: the comment service filters and appends to Kafka keyed by video_id, acks, and persister workers batch-insert into Cassandra
parts.why: 33k/s of tiny writes is easy for a partitioned log and painful for a single database. Making the log the only write removes the dual-write problem, and keying by video keeps each stream's comments in order for both consumers.

parts.title: Real-time delivery to viewers
parts.problem: 20M viewers on ~200 gateways must see new comments for the video they watch within 2 s, without the server doing work per viewer per comment.

options.name: Poll through the CDN every 2 s
options.pros: stateless; the CDN collapses identical requests per video
options.cons: ~10M requests/s at the edge, mostly empty; latency = poll interval + TTL

options.name: Per-viewer routing like chat (registry viewer → gateway)
options.cons: 5M registry lookups and sends per comment on a hot video

options.name: SSE gateways + pub/sub per video: each gateway subscribes once to every video its viewers watch and fans out in memory
options.pros: one publish per gateway, not per viewer; push latency is milliseconds
options.cons: stateful gateways; subscription churn when viewers zap between videos

parts.choice: SSE gateways that subscribe to a pub/sub channel per video once and fan batches out to their local viewers
parts.why: Fan-out cost becomes 'number of gateways with a viewer of this video' (≤ 200) instead of 'number of viewers' (up to 5M). Comments flow one way, so SSE over plain HTTP is enough; posting is a normal POST.

nodes.label: Dispatchers: batch + sample per video (500 ms)

parts.title: Hot stream: more comments than anyone can read
parts.problem: One stream has 5M viewers and 10k comments/s: that is 5 × 10^10 deliveries/s, and no human reads more than ~10 comments/s. One hot stream must not starve the others.

options.name: Deliver every comment to everyone
options.cons: 5 × 10^10 messages/s; unreadable on screen anyway

options.name: Send everything; let the client drop
options.cons: the network still carries 10k comments/s to 5M phones

options.name: Split viewers into rooms that only see their own room
options.cons: changes the product: viewers see different conversations

options.name: Batch + sample per video: every 500 ms the dispatcher publishes one batch of at most ~10 comments chosen by rules
options.pros: deliveries = viewers × 2/s regardless of comment rate; low-traffic videos still get every comment
options.cons: most comments on a hot stream are never shown live

parts.choice: Per-video dispatchers batch every 500 ms and sample down to ~10 comments per batch when the rate is high (keep verified, streamer and moderator comments first)
parts.why: Deliveries become 5M × 2 = 10M frames/s for the hottest stream and 40M/s overall, a bandwidth problem gateways can handle, and they stop growing with comment rate. Nothing a human could read is lost.

nodes.label: Dispatchers: batch + sample per video (500 ms)

parts.title: Recent comments for joiners
parts.problem: When a big stream starts, ~1M viewers join within a minute and each needs the last 50 comments immediately; all of them ask about the same video.

options.name: Query the comments table on each join
options.cons: ~17k reads/s on one partition: a hot partition

options.name: Redis list per video kept at 50 by the dispatcher
options.cons: one hot key per big video

options.name: Redis list behind a CDN with a 1 s TTL
options.pros: the edge absorbs the herd; the origin sees ~1 request/s per video per edge
options.cons: a joiner may miss up to a second of comments, which the live stream fills in

parts.choice: Dispatchers maintain a 50-item Redis list per video; GET /recent is served through the CDN with a 1 s TTL
parts.why: Every joiner of a video wants the same answer, so the response is perfectly cacheable for a second. That turns a hot key into a handful of origin reads, and the SSE stream covers the gap.

nodes.label: Dispatchers: batch + sample per video (500 ms)

deep_dives.title: Comment order on screen

options.name: client timestamps
options.cons: skewed clocks reorder comments and invite spoofing

options.name: global sequence
options.cons: a cross-video bottleneck for an order nobody can see

options.name: order within a video by log offset, time-ordered comment ids
options.pros: free from the partition keyed by video
options.cons: only per-video order, which is all a viewer sees

deep_dives.choice: order within a video by Kafka partition offset; comment ids are time-ordered for replay
deep_dives.why: A viewer only ever sees one video's comments, and the log already orders them per partition. Batches carry comments in offset order, so every viewer sees the same sequence.

deep_dives.title: Moderation and deletes

options.name: filter only on the client
options.cons: abusive text still reaches every phone

options.name: filter at post time + tombstone events for deletes
options.pros: bad words never enter the log; deletes reach screens via the same path
options.cons: the blocklist must be kept in sync on every comment service

deep_dives.choice: blocked-word filter in the comment service before the log; deletes are tombstone events that dispatchers publish and persisters apply
deep_dives.why: F4: deletes must vanish from screens within seconds, and the live path already reaches every viewer in < 2 s. The recent-comments list drops the id too, and the 1 s CDN TTL bounds staleness.

deep_dives.title: Gateway subscription churn

options.name: subscribe per viewer
options.cons: millions of subscriptions; pub/sub becomes per-viewer fan-out

options.name: subscribe per (gateway, video), reference-counted
options.cons: gateways track counts and unsubscribe when the last viewer leaves

deep_dives.why: Keeps the pub/sub layer's work bounded by ~200 gateways per video no matter how many viewers watch.

wrapup.bottlenecks: Gateway egress on hot streams (~80 GB/s overall), the single Kafka partition and dispatcher of the hottest video (10k/s is fine for one consumer, but watch it), the recent-comments key of a viral video (CDN in front).
wrapup.failures: Gateway crash: viewers reconnect with jitter and refetch recent comments. Dispatcher crash: another consumer takes the partition and resumes from the committed offset (a few duplicate batches are harmless). Redis pub/sub loss: gateways resubscribe; comments are already in the log. Persister lag: storage catches up, live view is unaffected.
wrapup.monitoring: Post → screen latency p99, comments/s and viewers per video, sampling ratio on hot streams, gateway connections and egress, Kafka consumer lag for dispatchers and persisters, CDN hit ratio for /recent.
wrapup.scale: More gateways and pub/sub shards (channel hashed by video); more Kafka partitions; for extreme events add a relay tier between pub/sub and gateways per region.
wrapup.future: Personalised sampling (always show friends' comments, added at the gateway), reactions as aggregated counters, replay synced to the video timeline.
